subject.title: fix(irc): disconnect on oversized inbound lines

question: Should OpenClaw make every inbound line over the classic 512-byte limit a fatal IRC disconnect, and if so, does that intentionally exclude IRCv3 extended message-tag lines and accept reconnect-loop behavior?
rationale: The resource bound is necessary, but choosing fatal disconnect versus bounded discard and deciding whether IRCv3 tag allowances are supported changes compatibility and channel availability; repository evidence does not establish that product contract.

options.title: Make the guard protocol-aware
options.body: Before merge, distinguish the IRCv3 tag section from the 512-byte message body and add coverage for overflow handling through the reconnecting monitor.

options.title: Approve strict classic IRC
options.body: Explicitly accept fatal disconnects for every whole line over 512 bytes, document that extended message-tag lines are unsupported, and prove reconnect backoff is bounded.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Leave the current behavior unchanged until an IRC owner defines the supported framing and reconnect contract.

recommendation.title: Make the guard protocol-aware
recommendation.body: Before merge, distinguish the IRCv3 tag section from the 512-byte message body and add coverage for overflow handling through the reconnecting monitor.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current IRC client and lifecycle implementation in the merged first-class channel work.
